quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Paralegals and legal assistants help lawyers by investigating facts, preparing legal documents and researching legal precedent.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Paralegals and Legal Assistants) include Legal Analyst, Legal Assistant, Law Associate, Litigation Paralegal and Paralegal.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Three (medium preparation needed): most occupations in this zone require training in vocational schools, related on-the-job experience, or an associate's degree.

sections.heading: What a paralegal does
paragraphs: Paralegals and legal assistants help lawyers by investigating facts, preparing legal documents and researching legal precedent.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Paralegals and Legal Assistants. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Prepare and review legal documents such as contracts, correspondence and affidavits.
Research statutes, decisions and other legal sources and summarise what they say.
Investigate the facts of a matter using public records and other sources.
Organise and maintain case and contract files so lawyers can find what they need.

sections.heading: How people get into this job

bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: LLB (Bachelor of Laws); B.A. LL.B. (Hons.).
Less common routes on the map: BA (Bachelor of Arts).
